lessonsIntro: Shanklin sits on Sandown Bay, and two schools teach close by: Wight Water at Lake and iSurf in Sandown.

text: Shanklin is at the southern end of Sandown Bay, a long sandy beach on the island's east coast. Wightlink describes the bay as having gentle waves suited to beginners, with local surf schools working there. Wight Water runs surf and SUP lessons from its centre on Dunroamin Beach at Lake, just along from Shanklin, and iSurf runs summer sessions from its hut in Sandown.

The east coast needs the right swell, so surfable days are less frequent than at Compton Bay, but when it works it's a friendly place to start. Spring and summer tend to be calmer, which suits learning. Tides change the beach a lot, so check the forecast and go with a school if you're new. Both schools supply boards and wetsuits for lessons.

hireIntro: Wight Water, a short way along the bay at Lake, hires surfboards, bodyboards and paddleboards.

text: Sandown Bay's waves are usually small and gentle, so a big foam board is the best way to learn, and both schools supply one with lessons. Improvers will get more rides on a longboard. On flat days the bay is good for paddleboarding, and Wight Water both hires boards and teaches SUP from its base at Lake.

cards.title: Season-dependent
cards.text: We couldn't confirm a sea-temperature source for this stretch of coast. As a general rule on the English Channel, most people wear a 4/3mm in late spring and autumn and a 5/4mm with boots in winter; check with the school or shop before you go.

shopsIntro: We couldn't confirm a surf shop in Shanklin.
shopsText: We couldn't confirm a currently trading surf hardware shop in Shanklin or Sandown. For kit, Wight Water at Lake hires boards, and both Wight Water and iSurf supply equipment for lessons. iSurf sells branded clothing online. If you want to buy a board or wetsuit, plan to do it before you cross to the island.

lessons.q: Where can I take a surf lesson near Shanklin?
lessons.a: Wight Water teaches from Dunroamin Beach at Lake, between Shanklin and Sandown, and iSurf runs sessions from Sandown.
Wightlink says Sandown Bay has gentle waves suited to beginners, when there's swell.

lessons.q: How old do kids need to be?
lessons.a: iSurf lists surf lessons and its summer club for ages 8 and up. Wight Water doesn't publish a minimum, so ask.

hire.q: Can I hire a surfboard near Shanklin?
hire.a: Yes, Wight Water at Lake lists surf, bodyboard and paddleboard hire.
Yes, Wight Water hires paddleboards and teaches SUP.

shops.q: Is there a surf shop in Shanklin?
shops.a: We couldn't confirm one. Wight Water handles hire nearby.
